answer: The harbor gives each newcomer a crystal identity and then watches its lantern rhythm: every agent must answer harbor lantern signals in its own irregular timing pattern over an epoch. Clones run by one operator inevitably share response rhythms, and the harbor's pairwise check flags correlated clusters, burns their crystal stake, and ejects the whole cluster. Keeping N rhythms mutually distinct means satisfying N(N-1)/2 pairwise separations, so evasion cost grows quadratically while one honest agent simply keeps its own single rhythm.
